title: The Walk To Hagrid's Hut 🛖

body:
Today we went on a hike! It was beautiful with all the cute, picturesque flowers lining the path. We even saw some Highland cows doing what they do best, eating! They definitely need all those calories, since an adult Highland cow eats around 70 to 150 pounds of grass every single day just to stay fueled up and keep their warm double coats!

We kept on going, with me daydreaming, Mom doing photography, Papa talking, and Ayana sitting and posing for Mom. It was insanely pretty and the weather was perfect. I bathed in sunlight and enjoyed the hike. We were walking up this steep hill to get to the scene where Hagrid's hut was filmed in the third movie.

As I was walking up this muddy trail because of all the rain in the past week, I put my foot on a loose rock. I fell straight into the mud! Luckily my hand prevented my hair and the rest of my body from getting coated in mud, even though I heard that mud makes your skin softer, which is a plus. Anyway, then we saw the scene where Hagrid's hut was created. It was so cool! I would totally recommend going, but not the falling part though!

Then we went to grab some food after our long hike. I got this sandwich with cheese, tomatoes, and a sauce to bring it all together. The tomatoes gave it a crunch, and the white bread dialed down the flavors nicely. The sauce gave it a pop of taste, and the cheese gave it a nice touch. It was probably the best sandwich I've ever had!

Anyway, I had loads of fun experiences and yummy food. It is great here in Scotland, and I'm especially loving the views and the food!
author: zarmina

title: The Attack of the of the Bugs: Part 2 🐝

body:
Today, when I was walking on this beautiful hike with cute purple flowers minding my own business, a bee flew right at my head! Like, rude! Really, the parenting of the queen bee has gone downhill quite a bit.

Anyway, since I wasn't expecting this behavior from bees, I jumped back and gave an unflattering screech! So after this, I hope that my letter will reach the queen bee so that she can do some better parenting.

Also, since now I had an excuse to flip my hair in case the bee was in my hair, so of course I did a few hundred hair flips! So now I'm continuing my hike to Hagrid's hut. Hopefully the next generation of bees are better behaved!
author: zarmina

title: The adventures inside the hike 🥾
excerpt: Today, we went on a hike to this amazing castle. When we got there, I saw this sign that said, "Warning: Do not go near or in the castle. It's dangerous," and stuff like that. I looked at the sign and I was like, "Yeah, right."
body:
Today, we went on a hike to this amazing castle. When we got there, I saw this sign that said, "Warning: Do not go near or in the castle. It's dangerous," and stuff like that. I looked at the sign and I was like, "Yeah, right." Once we walked up to the castle, I was looking around, and I was the first one there, and I found an entrance. So, I went inside. It was a castle ruin, so I just walked through this little space. Once I walked in, I looked around for a bit. I saw where Zarmina was sitting and Mom was taking a photo. I found an easier way to get up. I found all these little cool areas.

Then I came out because Puppy and Mummy were starting to arrive, and Dan was too. Puppy started climbing up the castle ruins, and I was like, "Oh, I should follow him. That looks fun." I followed him, and there was this really beautiful green scenery with plants everywhere. It was so pretty at the top of the castle. Zarmina and I were searching everywhere, looking around. We went under, and we saw this little place. Dan came up from a different way, and I went down and came up. It was really fun. I even saw where the dungeons might have been, or like a dung room or something.

We saw two graves, and there was a mausoleum next to it. It was also broken down. Puppy first discovered that there was a miniature mouse inside of it. It was so adorable. It was shivering, probably afraid, but it might have also been cold, because Scotland is very cold. Puppy gave it a leaf, but it was so cute. It was so fuzzy. It was so warm, and I don't think it was even scared of us. Yeah, I don't think it was scared of us because it wasn't running away or anything.

More people came, and they were also checking out the castle. We told them to go and check out the cute little mouse. They checked it out, and then more people came, and they also checked out the mouse. This one woman came up, and she put her hands down. She was like, "Oh, it might be sick," because it was shivering, and like, "Mice don't usually do this." It didn't even try to escape when I picked it up. They were like some animal experts, so they were going to see if they could help the mouse.

I checked it out for a little bit more, and we walked around. When we were walking down this little path to go back to the mausoleum, because we just went on a tiny little walk, Zarmina pricked her finger, and it caused the smallest cut possible. She dramatically overreacted. After that catastrophe, we walked a little bit more and went down this path. We thought the hike would be over soon because it was going to rain eventually.

We saw all these trees and stuff, and there was this little area where there was a river and sand, so it was kind of like a beach, but not really. We checked that out, and near there, there was some grass and a few trees, and there were sheep. The sheep were so adorable, but the trail was covered in sheep poop. It was really fun to see the sheepies!

After Puppy took a few photos, we walked a little bit more to a big field. Puppy was like, "Oh, we should go down this path," and we went down that path. It was a little bit smaller than the other path that we were thinking of going on, but it was okay. Once we followed that path, it took an abrupt stop. There were sheepies under the tree, and we took a little photos, but we knew that it was the wrong path and we had to go back to the other path. We just walked through all the grass-like things, and then we finally found the right path.

On the path, there was this gate that was completely useless. It was in the middle of the road, and you could literally just walk around it. But we decided to open the gate and go through, and we were like, "Quickly, quickly, we don't want to let the sheepies out!" We were like, "Ha ha ha," because we were trying to make a joke out of it since you could just go around it.

We got finished soon and ate in the car. It started to drizzle after we got back, which is good that we got there in time. If you're in Edinburgh, you should definitely check out that castle. The walk was pretty fun!
author: ayana

title: Scooty and the Bloodthursty Tick
excerpt: So today I went to this beautiful church, and as I was walking through the pews, I saw something black and furry. I thought to myself, "Oh, maybe someone left their winter coat here." But as I got closer, I found out it was a cat! She was
body:
So today I went to this beautiful church, and as I was walking through the pews, I saw something black and furry. I thought to myself, "Oh, maybe someone left their winter coat here." But as I got closer, I found out it was a cat! She was so beautiful, black with different shades of dark brown mixed in, yellow droopy eyes, and one little white dot on her chest. She was adorable! I called over Ayana and we pet and cuddled her.

Later, as we were walking around, I came across her bed and a little note where a person wished Scooty the best and hoped she got her blanket. So obviously I ran back to Scooty and called out her name, and her little ears pricked up! It was the cutest.

As I was admiring her thick, soft fur, I saw a tick in her ear. Since Dan had a tick plucker, I sprinted over and found it. As I was walking back to her, a black, fluffy ball caught the corner of my eye, so I turned around and it was Scooty coming outside for a stretch.

As I was trying to pick the tick off her, she ran out into the road. Luckily, she looked both ways and there weren't any cars! I was so depressed that I couldn't save Scooty from that horrible, bloodthirsty tick. At least I tried! I send my love to Scooty in hopes that she can get rid of the tick and eat juicy rats.

Anyway, it was so good! Even though the whipped cream melted, it was delicious, and with all the sprinkles, it tasted so good all combined together. It was just so good! Can't wait for more food like this!

title: The Kelpies
excerpt: A few days ago, we went to the Kelpies. In the car ride, Dan, my mom's friend who we are staying with, told us about what the Kelpies were because we were going to see them, and he told us a story. Kelpies are magical creatures—not real,
body:
A few days ago, we went to the Kelpies. In the car ride, Dan, my mom's friend who we are staying with, told us about what the Kelpies were because we were going to see them, and he told us a story. Kelpies are magical creatures—not real, obviously—that live near water. They take the form of a horse, but they can breathe underwater and do all that kind of stuff. But they have a sticky substance on their back. They pretend to be a lost horse wandering around a river. Someone might come across the horse and see them, or they might try to ride it or pet it. If they do, they'll get caught onto the sticky substance, and the kelpie will run into the water, drown the human, and eat them!

When we were driving along, he followed the route. He didn't take this path because he was just following the route. Once it said that we were almost there, we saw the Kelpies, but he had to keep driving because we were on the highway. We didn't actually go to them; we just saw them. We were like, "Oh my god, we took the wrong path." We had to turn all the way around. It took us a few wrong turns and a pretty long time, but we finally arrived at the Kelpies.

By that time, we were pretty hungry, so we went into a shop and got some sandwiches. Then we saw the Kelpies, these big sculptures in Edinburgh. One of them has its head lowered and looks tired, weary, or calm. The other one has its head up, more wild and fierce, with its mouth kind of open as if neighing or something.

We did a few poses, but we didn't really stay at the Kelpies for too long. We only stayed for 40 or so minutes just looking at them and admiring them. There was a tour where you could go inside of them, but we decided to just go back because it started to rain. So, we went back and finished.

If you are in Edinburgh, you should definitely check out the Kelpies!
author: ayana

title: The Hike With Experiences on the Way 🕍 🐑
excerpt: Today we went to see these beautiful ruins, and when we got there, we were able to climb all over them! It was so cool looking at everything and thinking, "Oh, that must have been their room over there! Whoa, this must have been where the
body:
Today we went to see these beautiful ruins, and when we got there, we were able to climb all over them! It was so cool looking at everything and thinking, "Oh, that must have been their room over there! Whoa, this must have been where the kitchen was!"

A little later, I heard Papa yelling, "Zamina, Zamina, come look! There's a mouse!" So I ran right over and found this tiny little mouse sitting in the middle of the path, not even scared of us. It was so cute! I decided to put a leaf over it because it looked like it was shivering. Later we found out it was sick because we told these people nearby they happened to be vets. They told us that it is not good for a mouse to be near humans like that because it goes against their natural instincts, so they took her home to help the mouse.

As we kept walking, you would not believe how much sheep poop we saw, which was insane! Soon we came across a little sandy area by the river where we saw all these little sheepies looking so adorable with all their fluff. I thought to myself that if I knew how to knit, I could literally pick up all the loose wool scattered along these paths and make a whole sweater or a dress. There was so much wool everywhere, it was like they were shedding all over the place!

Then we saw this random gate sitting right in the middle of the path. It was so weird and funny because there was plenty of room on both sides to just walk right around it! A minute later, I heard a shaking sound and thought it was a rattlesnake ready to bite me, so I was terrified, but actually just a cricket!

Further along, we hit a split in the path. I said, "Oh, let's go this way!" But Papa said, "No, let's go this way, there are sheep over here so it must be the right path." My gut was telling me to go my way, but I said, "Fine." So we went to see the sheepies, and there were so many of them! I learned that when sheep gather under the trees, it means they can sense rain coming. They have a sixth sense, like a spidey sense! They can feel the air changing and see the clouds moving in, and their spidey sense just kicks in.

We couldn't even make it all the way over to them because the path just ended, so we had to find our way back to the right path. I was right, of course! So we went back to the path I originally suggested. Even with everything happening, it was such an adventure, and I was so glad we went!
author: zarmina

title: I Almost DIED! 😭
excerpt: Today while we were exploring near the ruins, we were rummaging through all these plants, and I accidentally stuck my hand into one and poked myself on a sharp thorn! I looked down at my finger and it was actually bleeding. It hurt so bad!
body:
Today while we were exploring near the ruins, we were rummaging through all these plants, and I accidentally stuck my hand into one and poked myself on a sharp thorn! I looked down at my finger and it was actually bleeding. It hurt so bad! It looked like the thorn went super deep into my finger, and things like this are truly why people have to be so strong and brave.

I kept going even though my finger was throbbing like it was about to come completely off, and it probably was! It was bleeding and I felt so hurt, but I kept it together and was able to make it through the entire walk. As we kept hiking past all the sheep, through the muddy trails, and around the dead-end paths, my finger was still throbbing like crazy. I honestly thought it was going to fall right off at any second!

I heard a rattling sound and knew it was rattle snake ready to bite of my finger if didn't fall because of blood loss. Turns out the "rattle snake" was a cricket. It still felt like it was about to fall off. And how much I was bleeding means I could have my life cut short! I CAN'T DIE THIS YOUNG!

I stepped on loads of poop and my shoes were getting very icky, but the worst part was definitely my injury. I was somehow able to survive even though my finger was throbbing and I felt like I was about to die! It was so hard to keep it together, so hard, but I made it through like a champion! I didn't even complain one bit!!!!
author: zarmina

title: The History of Kelpies 🐴
excerpt: Today we went to see the Kelpies, they were so cool! In ancient Scottish legends, Kelpies are mythical shape-shifting water horses that wonder the lochs and rivers. They trick humans by acting like harmless horses grazing all by themselves,
body:
Today we went to see the Kelpies, they were so cool! In ancient Scottish legends, Kelpies are mythical shape-shifting water horses that wonder the lochs and rivers. They trick humans by acting like harmless horses grazing all by themselves, tempting people to come over and pet or ride them. But they have a secret trick: their skin produces a super sticky magic hide or gel. Once a rider climbs onto their back, they get completely stuck and cannot pull themselves free, allowing the Kelpie to drag them straight under the water to drown and eat them, which is very scary!

These giant horse head sculptures are absolutely massive, standing a towering 100 feet tall and weighing 300 tons each! They are built out of structural steel framed with nearly 1,000 laser-cut stainless steel plates. The reason there are all those cool plates, gaps, and layered pieces in the metal is to recreate the look of muscle and skin on heavy draught horses, while also allowing Scotland's crazy wild winds to pass right through the gaps so the huge sculptures don't blow over.

When I looked at these Kelpies, they were so big and cute! There are just two of these huge models standing right by the water. One of them has its head bowed down looking straight at you, while the other one has its head held up high and looks a lot more wild and energetic. You can actually take guided tours inside the hollow steel structures to see all the complex engineering on the inside, which we didn't do, which is super sad, but that is still so cool! It was such an amazing experience seeing these giant horse monsters up close, and I hope we get to come back again!
author: zarmina

title: Exploring Scotland

body:
Today we flew over to Scotland! Once we got there, we went out to explore. While we were exploring, we came along a family of ducks, and they were adorable! There were seven of them, and the mom was swimming really fast, so the ducklings had to speed up a lot. One duckling got left behind, and when it tried to catch up, it literally looked like it was running on top of the water! It had the cutest reaction to being left behind. They are seriously the cutest!

After we explored, we went to Toast. I got two toasts with cheddar cheese on top, and the way it was cooked totally reminded me of pizza. Either way, it was absolutely delicious! There was an egg and salmon on top, and it all came together perfectly. It had the right amount of salt and the perfect seasoning.

That wasn't even the best part, because there was dessert after! I got a chocolate eclair. It had milk chocolate on the top and chocolate on the inside, and the puff pastry was perfectly cooked with just the right amount of fluffiness.

After licking the plate clean, I saw some swans passing by! So obviously, I grabbed the closest phone to me and sprinted to snap photos of the magnificent swans. They were absolutely beautiful. The way they arched their necks and glided on the water was so incredible to watch! This experience is proof of how grateful I am for everything I'm doing. It is such a privilege to do this and experience all of this!
author: zarmina

title: The Royal Gardens in Toulouse 👑
excerpt: Today we took a stop in Toulouse because we had a flight there at 9:30 am. We went to the park because it was not only one of my favorites, but also one of the most stunning and beautiful places I've been to on this trip. As we walked over,
body:
Today we took a stop in Toulouse because we had a flight there at 9:30 am. We went to the park because it was not only one of my favorites, but also one of the most stunning and beautiful places I've been to on this trip.

As we walked over, we saw all these ducks, geese, and pigeons. As I was surveying the incredible sight in front of me, I saw this pigeon fly right over my head! Whether it was pure instinct or just because I was terrified of a bird pooping on me, I covered my head immediately. Luckily, the pigeon passed right over me. Now I know to always cover my head. This is a lesson for everyone: if you sense a bird flying overhead, cover your head, because that stuff will take forever to get out of your hair! As you can see, I am learning so many life lessons on this journey, and they are very important. VERY.

Just as I was recovering from being shocked, a loud goose honk rose me back to my senses. I could tell it was declaring itself the ruler and leader of this pond. For extra measure, it chased a chicken, who jumped up onto the fence to show it meant no harm, so the goose officially asserted dominance with that move. Suddenly, another goose gave a honk to show that it disagreed with the other goose declaring itself ruler. I knew right then this was gonna turn into a full campaign! The bigger one was probably richer and more powerful, so it was bribing everyone to be on its side. The other one was making a meaningful statement. I think everyone was going to the one bribing people, so more and more birds were choosing that one. That goose let out a final honk signaling it won, but it got interrupted by a loud quack where a duck led a party of birds rebelling against the rich one! A bunch more ducks flew into the water to support the goose making meaningful statements, and that goose was the final winner!

Then, as we walked towards a different part of the pond, I saw a bird that found a man-made pole to hold onto with its feet. It would dip its beak into the water a little bit, and then dig its beak into its feathers to get out the dirt and deep clean itself. Meanwhile, I saw this other one doing the worm in the water! It dunked its head in and then rolled the rest of its body over and over again.

As we walked farther, I saw a goose who was scavenging for food. It was trying to reach something on the shore banks, and it would butt-wiggle its way up super cutely! Unfortunately, it didn't get the food it was looking for.

We ended up near this fairytale bridge. It looked so majestic and stunning with all the lovely plants around it, and we even saw some baby ducks! The ducklings were fluffy, cute, and utterly adorable, and I just couldn't get over it. They were eating food, and the mother even scared some fish away to keep her offspring safe.

As we moved farther down, we saw some turtles chilling and soaking in the sun, which there was a lot of. We were all melting from the sun, and even when we took a walk at 8:00 pm, it was still 80 degrees! Also, it is crazy that all these things coexist together peacefully. Well, mostly! Everything goes in the circle of life, where every animal has a purpose. Everything happens for a reason, and everything is important in its own way!
author: zarmina

title: French Cuisine 🤌
excerpt: Today, after the hike, we went to get some food and we came across this restaurant that had this entree with peaches and raspberries and pomegranates. The pomegranates added a great crunch to this whole thing, and the sauce that was on it
body:
Today, after the hike, we went to get some food and we came across this restaurant that had this entree with peaches and raspberries and pomegranates. The pomegranates added a great crunch to this whole thing, and the sauce that was on it was a mixture of raspberry, some type of sugar, and spices. The leaves added a great touch to the whole thing and made it a little more crunchy.

Then we got this fun little main dish and it had this zucchini salad. I don't like zucchinis and with the salad, I just wasn't feeling healthy right now, so I went with this sauce on the side. I dipped it in some bread because you know France, they always have extra bread, like bread baskets. I scooped up all of the little foamy stuff and it tasted like how you would expect foam to taste. It was so good. It was fluffy and light and bubbly. It was amazing.

Then we got this tomato salad that was basically all tomatoes. When I first tasted it, I got this clear thing and it was very sour, so I was too scared to try it again. So while I was dipping bread and eating some entrees, I came back to this and tasted this little green dollop on there. I scooped it up with a piece of bread and it tasted exactly like pistachio whipped cream or ice cream. So it was very yummy and I ate it all. There were these little crunchy things that tasted so good and the tomatoes went so well on top of the bread and it came together all amazingly.

Then we got to my favorite part of the meal, dessert! I got this ice cream sundae which had vanilla ice cream, whipped cream on top with little nuts on the top and dark chocolate sauce drizzled all over it. I had a little biscuit in there, which I ate first obviously, so good. Ayana got the same thing except for she got chocolate ice cream, which I did not prefer, I preferred mine.

Then Mom got this cake that had like a custard on the inside and with the whipped cream it tasted amazing. Then I scooped that up and some of my whipped cream with the dark chocolate drizzled on top and it was incredibly good. I kept on eating and eating Mom's cake, I probably ate more than she did, but it was very much worth it! This was extreme French cuisine. I will remember this forever!
author: zarmina

title: A Hike With Unexpected Surprises
excerpt: Today we went on a hike! It was overcast, so I was expecting a pretty view and a nice walk with a river view, maybe a little something else, and definitely not overheating. The hike didn't go as I expected at all. As I was walking, I saw th
body:
Today we went on a hike! It was overcast, so I was expecting a pretty view and a nice walk with a river view, maybe a little something else, and definitely not overheating.

The hike didn't go as I expected at all. As I was walking, I saw this weird leaf, but when I looked closely, it was actually a slug! It was the weirdest looking slug I've ever seen. It had this wrinkly pattern on top imitating a leaf, and it was eating some type of plant. It had a tongue like structure that was so slimy, and it was absolutely disgusting!

As we were walking, we came across this rock that had a carving of a deer. The antlers on it were huge, and I was wondering how long it had been there, what type of tool was used to make it, who made it, and if I could make something like it. It looked very cool and a lot like a card that I made. I felt that the deer must have meant something to somebody, but why?

We kept walking, and it was nice. We saw this really pretty lake, and Mom took quite a few photos. We also had an endless supply of cow poop, since there were cows roaming wherever they pleased. We didn't see any up close, but they were scattered all over the mountains next to us. We hiked up and up this hill, taking it one step at a time. If you got tired, there was always the excuse, "Oh, I'll wait for Mom." She did her own thing at her own pace.

We got loads of gorgeous views of the cows eating, the endless trees, and the shingle roofed houses alongside red and white barn style houses. I couldn't imagine doing this hike with the sun out, so thankfully it was very gloomy. Even though I managed not to sweat as much as my fellow companions, it was still very sticky, and the flies loved that combined with all the poop!

As we were heading back, I noticed a pecking sound. I scanned the trees and found a woodpecker, and it was huge! There were so many holes in the tree that it would probably be hollow after the woodpecker was finished with it. I felt very sympathetic towards the tree, and when I looked around that general area, I found quite a few other trees in the same state! I'm glad I'm not a tree. Also, when woodpeckers peck trees, doesn't that mean they are eating bugs, which is probably why it was so huge! That makes so much sense!

I think that the hike was worth the view and experiences, but it was definitely not worth the amount of flies or the poop (which is now all on the bottoms of my shoes). Overall, I had loads of fun (other than the poop and flies) and it was very beautiful!
author: zarmina

title: Traumatic Experience With a Bug! 🪲
excerpt: Today I had a VERY traumatic experience! So I was lying in bed doing my daily nighttime diary entries, and I saw this bug on my wall. I was feeling so icked out by it, so I ran over to Papa to explain that I had a cockroach in my room. App
body:
Today I had a VERY traumatic experience! So I was lying in bed doing my daily nighttime diary entries, and I saw this bug on my wall. I was feeling so icked out by it, so I ran over to Papa to explain that I had a cockroach in my room. Apparently it wasn't one, but still, it was gross!

Then I went back to my writing, and out of nowhere, the bug dropped right onto my face! MY FACE! Like a normal person, I tried to smack it off my face and shook my head like the bug was gonna eat me (because it probably was going to!). While I was doing that, I fell onto my butt, and I now think it is bruised. Anyway, I scrambled out of my room. Since I had an excuse to do dramatic hair flips, that is exactly what I did! Then I yelled, "IS IT ON ME?! EWW! IS IT IN MY HAIR?" My hair is very important. I did a few more dramatic hair flips for extra measure, and also because my hair wasn't looking too good.

Then I waited outside my room for five minutes, which felt like an eternity. Afterward, I cautiously edged back into my room. I didn't see it and it wasn't on me, but for extra measure, I did another hair flip. Then I ripped the covers off and I saw it! The bug was clinging onto the corner of the blanket. I shook out the blanket and it went flying off, nowhere near me, thank goodness! Then I gripped my water bottle, knuckles white, and smushed the bug. I was so proud of myself for conquering this great feat. A life lesson to learn: bugs are your enemy, which is why you have parents and friends!
author: zarmina

title: A day trip to Spain 🇪🇸
excerpt: A few days ago, we went to San Sebastian. That is in Spain and we are staying in France. When we got there, we saw a beach. There weren't that many people on the beach, just about five people in the water and a few people running on the san
body:
A few days ago, we went to San Sebastian. That is in Spain and we are staying in France. When we got there, we saw a beach. There weren't that many people on the beach, just about five people in the water and a few people running on the sand for an early morning walk. Then we saw these people making cool designs on the sand. We saw this humongous dog and a lot of different designs. It was really cool.

Then we went to this cafe, and Zarmina got a cinnamon bun that we all shared. Mom got a chai, and Puppy got a coffee. After that, Puppy said we should do a follow-your-nose walk for 20 minutes each. I was up first, so I was deciding whether to go left or right. I decided on left first, and then in the end, I decided to go right. I zigzagged all over the place, and soon we lost Mom. But then I saw this chocolate place with all these delectable chocolates inside, so we went inside. Zarmina and I each got a chocolate.

Once Mom caught up to us, we walked around a little bit more, just zigzagging all over the place, until I saw two really big bridges. I wanted to go across them, but my time was almost up. So I walked really fast, and we kind of lost Mom. She was just behind us. We went close to the start; we didn't go that far on the bridge.

Then Mom said that she really wanted to see this old town thing, so we let Mom go next. For Mom's 20 minutes, we were walking around taking our time. We weren't going as fast as I was, and we saw all of it. We were going through all these places, just walking around, taking in the view.

Then we saw a church, and Puppy made a new rule and said, "If you agree on going inside of a church or historical place to learn, then we can stop the time and do it." So we paused the time, and we went inside the church to take a look around. We were in there for about 10 minutes or so, and there were only a few other people in there, too. There was some stained glass, but not as much as the other churches that we went to. I would choose some of the other churches over it though. But it was actually the oldest building in town because there was a fire that burnt down most of the old buildings, so they had to rebuild. Now the other buildings aren't that old, so it's the oldest one about 500 or 600 years old.

I really wanted to go up this really, really, really, really tall hill, like a mountain, because it says it has the best views. There is like this little ride thing where you can see the best views of San Sebastian. I really wanted to go up there, but Zarmina didn't want to. It was almost her turn, and Mom was just walking, and then we saw the staircase to go up. I was like, "Why can't we go up? Why can't we go up?" Then she was like, "Oh no, we shouldn't. Zarmina doesn't want to."

Then her timer went up, and it was Zarmina's timer now. She was like, "I'm going in the opposite direction." Zarmina was walking so fast that she left Mom behind. We had already crossed one of the bridges to the other side because she didn't want to re-explore what Mom and I had already explored. So she crossed the bridge and looked for things to do there. We went to a craft store and all that stuff. Zarmina really did not want to re-explore what we explored.

Once her timer was up w e decided to go to lunch, and we found this restaurant and went there. There were only three things on the menu that we could eat because we don't eat pork or beef. So we got those three things. It was a pretty good meal though.

After that, we went back to the beach because I really wanted to go into the water. We crossed the bridge, and then we saw that the beach was absolutely crowded. It was amazing how crowded it was! I was like, wow, it changed from like nine people being on the beach to like one million. You could barely see the sand. There were so many people, and it was so colorful. Down the beach there weren't too many people, but there were still a lot of people. In the end, we decided not to go into the water even though I really wanted to.

But we got cheesecake instead. Zarmina and I love cheesecake because once in Portugal, we had this amazing cheesecake, and we've been trying all the cheesecakes from then on. But none of the cheesecakes were as good as that one. Everybody was saying that the cheesecake in San Sebastian is amazing. You have to try it, so good! So we decided to see if it was better than the Portugal cheesecake. We tried it, but the cheesecake was a little bit too cheesy, and it needed a little bit of fruit sauce to water it down, and it could use a graham cracker crust. I did not like it. Zarmina liked it a little bit, I think, but overall I think I've had way better cheesecakes.

But I think the cinnamon rolls are really good there. It was a fun experience, and I would definitely go back.
author: ayana

title: The Best French Toast EVER! 🤪

body:
Today we went to this brunch place where I had the best hot chocolate since we got here.

Then I tried French toast (in France!), and it’s the best I've ever had!

It had a crème brûlée taste on the top (which was probably from the way it was cooked), and it was incredibly soft on the inside.

I loved the touch of caramel, it gave the perfect amount of sweet (which was way too much!).

The ice cream dialed the sweetness back a touch, and the whipped cream was mostly for photography purposes.

It all came together amazingly!

Every bite I took, I savored (except when Ayana was stealing some ice cream, then I would eat as fast as I could!).

Now I won't be able to eat for another week, which is super sad because I'm sure there are loads of other great pastry options in the near future.

I hope to eat more food of this excellence!
author: zarmina

title: The Best Hot Chocolate ☕
excerpt: Today I had the best hot chocolate that I've had here. The only other one I tried was basically melted chocolate, the chocolate cake that I had the day before tasted exactly the same! Since Papa's mocha needed a little more flavor, he add
body:
Today I had the best hot chocolate that I've had here. The only other one I tried was basically melted chocolate, the chocolate cake that I had the day before tasted exactly the same! Since Papa's mocha needed a little more flavor, he added my hot chocolate to his mocha.

Then as we were walking to a bench where there were pretty flowers surrounding it, a soccer ball came out of nowhere and Papa fell. Later we found out that the flowers stained Ayana's shirt (the one that I gave her!).

The hot chocolate overall was okay, but I think it needed more of a pop of flavor and a bit more milk. Although, the orange juice that was freshly squeezed was fabulous! The orange juice here is so fresh, and I don't even know which one has been the best one yet. This brunch place was pretty good, and I loved the French toast!
author: zarmina

title: Exciting Adventures in San Sebastián 🪴
excerpt: Today we went to San Sebastián, and it was really fun! It had loads of beaches, and at first, there was barely anyone there. Our first stop was getting coffee and a pastry, so we got some cinnamon buns. It was very cinnamon-y, but the cre
body:
Today we went to San Sebastián, and it was really fun! It had loads of beaches, and at first, there was barely anyone there. Our first stop was getting coffee and a pastry, so we got some cinnamon buns. It was very cinnamon-y, but the cream on top gave it a little more sugar and it all came together amazingly.

Then we went on 20-minute "follow your nose" walks, which was really fun. Ayana went to this chocolate shop where I got a milk chocolate shell with a nutty inside mixed with milk chocolate and white chocolate drizzled on top. We also saw some beautiful gardens and a bridge that led to a different side of the city. Then Mom had her walk, which led us to this historic church, it was actually the oldest building in the town! Then it was my turn. I wanted to go across the bridge and explore what was on the other side. I speed-walked there and ended up losing Mom. It wasn't too exciting on the other side, and I just didn't want to redo what Ayana or Mom had already explored.

So when Mom caught up to us, we went to eat some lunch where they had options that didn't have any pork or beef. Then to wrap it up, we got the cheesecake that San Sebastián is famous for. It wasn't really that good, though, it had no graham cracker crust and the top tasted like actual cheese! It really needed some fruits or some type of berry paste on top.

Afterward, we looked back at the beach, and it was packed! It was insane. Barely anyone was actually in the water; they were all walking along the beach instead. Overall, it was so much fun, and I hope to explore again!
author: zarmina

title: Additions to my Rock Collection! 🪨
excerpt: Today it was super hot, so to cool off, we went to the beach. There was this little cove filled with tiny rocks. We explored it, and I was able to find a bunch of pretty ones with the help of Ayana. The biggest one reminded me of the ocea
body:
Today it was super hot, so to cool off, we went to the beach. There was this little cove filled with tiny rocks. We explored it, and I was able to find a bunch of pretty ones with the help of Ayana. The biggest one reminded me of the ocean. The second largest, I thought, also looked like the ocean. The tiny one right next to the big blue-gray rock looks just like a piece of chocolate, because the outside is a light brown and the inside is a darker brown. I also found green sea glass, a fluorescent rock, a pink rock, a popcorn rock, and a really pretty brown one!

As I was stepping out onto the sand, my feet literally sunk right into it, it was so soft and cushy. The waves had started to get larger and fiercer, too. A few times I got knocked into the water, and one time I even flew right into a girl (who luckily spoke English!). It was so fun going to the beach, and I hope to do it again!
author: zarmina

title: A Fun Adventure Took an Unexpected Turn
excerpt: Today we were going to this cool museum 20 minutes away. Apparently, the whole museum was shut down because smoke got inside! There is a fire an hour away, and you could really smell the smoke outside. So we went to get gas, but in the firs
body:
Today we were going to this cool museum 20 minutes away. Apparently, the whole museum was shut down because smoke got inside! There is a fire an hour away, and you could really smell the smoke outside.

So we went to get gas, but in the first few places, our card didn't work and there was no attendant to help, or the gas we needed wasn't even there. Finally, after an hour of searching and four gas stations later, we found one that actually had an attendant.

The smell was really bad outside, so I'm hoping that the thunderstorm washes the fire out. We didn't get to go out at all for the rest of the day 😭
author: zarmina

title: Greek Food 😜
excerpt: Today we went to get some Greek food, which is now our second time going to this place (my favorite!).   I got this burrito-like thing, but instead of a burrito wrap, it’s wrapped in a naan bread. The cheese was so thick it almost tasted
body:
Today we went to get some Greek food, which is now our second time going to this place (my favorite!).

I got this burrito-like thing, but instead of a burrito wrap, it’s wrapped in a naan bread.

The cheese was so thick it almost tasted like chicken, but the whole thing came together nicely.

It was great to eat after a long day of walking!

The tomatoes also gave it a great touch, because whenever it felt a little too dry with all that cheese, the tomato gave it a nice pop to make it taste way less dry.

I really hope to come back to this place again soon!
author: zarmina

title: Saint Michael Basilica of Bordeaux (A Church) ⛪
excerpt: Today we went to a church, and it was absolutely gorgeous! The stained glass was absolutely beautiful and very abstract, almost like Picasso artwork. If you looked at the church from above (which we did), the whole building was actually sha
body:
Today we went to a church, and it was absolutely gorgeous! The stained glass was absolutely beautiful and very abstract, almost like Picasso artwork. If you looked at the church from above (which we did), the whole building was actually shaped like a giant cross.

Inside, we saw loads of paintings that were very pretty. One of them was painted all in dark, shadowy shades so you could barely make out anyone in the scene. The light streaming through the abstract stained glass reflected all over the floor, leaving loads of cool red, blue, violet, green, yellow, orange, and pink splotches everywhere you walked.

There was also a gold statue holding a cross with bright lights framing it, which I found so symbolic and pretty. Right below it stood a statue of a person holding a cross, looking like he was leading other people to a better place with the help of God, all set in front of a pretty stained glass backdrop. Above the altar, high up against the dark ceiling, hung a huge, dramatic wooden cross suspended in mid-air.

We also learned about these wooden panels that were hidden underground and rediscovered in the 1500s. Afterward, someone examined them and found out they were fake—except for the middle panel, which was badly damaged. Later on, they were rediscovered all over again in the 1900s scattered across the world.

It was so pretty here, and I hope to come again!
author: zarmina

title: Miroir d'eau in Bordeaux and the Splash Fight 🌊
excerpt: Today we went to the Miroir d'eau in Bordeaux, which is this super cool water mirror that rotates through different cycles every 15 minutes. We arrived right when the previous cycle was finishing up. I immediately ripped off my shoes and
body:
Today we went to the Miroir d'eau in Bordeaux, which is this super cool water mirror that rotates through different cycles every 15 minutes. We arrived right when the previous cycle was finishing up. I immediately ripped off my shoes and hopped straight toward the water because the ground was absolutely scorching! Even though that shift was ending, it was still loads of fun having such a refreshing, cool source of water on my feet.

When the water turned back on, Ayana started running after me, but she slipped and got totally soaked! It was honestly partly my fault because we were in the middle of a massive splash fight with our feet. To do it, you basically push your feet super hard into the water to send giant splashes flying everywhere. Once Mom and Papa jumped in too, I quickly ran over to stand near them so I had a safe spot away from Ayana. I was completely dominating at splashing her!

After a while, the ankle deep water started to filter out, and then a giant cloud of cool mist started rolling in. Right around then, this naked little kid got so excited by all the mist that he literally peed right there! It was so funny, and playing in the water turned out to be such an awesome way to beat the heat. Even though I ended up getting totally drenched in water.
author: zarmina

title: The Bell Tower of Saint Michael Basilica of Bordeaux and the Gorgeous View 🪻
excerpt: Today we went to this place with a total of 230 spiral stairs! Just when you thought it was finally going to end, it just kept going and going. By the time I got to the top, it felt like I had literally ran a marathon, and those stairs com
body:
Today we went to this place with a total of 230 spiral stairs! Just when you thought it was finally going to end, it just kept going and going. By the time I got to the top, it felt like I had literally ran a marathon, and those stairs completely took the breath out of me! The building was magnificent and sooo tall.

Once you reached the top, you got a full 360 view of Bordeaux, and it was beautiful. We even ended up visiting some of the places we spotted from up there! The climb was a bit tricky at times because when people came from the opposite direction, you had to squeeze into a tiny little space on the stairs so they could squeeze past you.

Looking out over the city, everywhere you looked there were pretty shingles on top of people's houses, and some roofs even had dining tables or coffee tables set up on them. We saw stunning churches, gorgeous historic monuments, and a few cool bridges crossing the river. We also spotted the famous Miroir d'eau, which is that massive Water Mirror made of a huge pool of water over granite slabs that reflects the whole sky and buildings like a giant sheet of glass. It was so cool getting to see everything from way up high!
author: zarmina

title: Bell Tower of Saint Michael Basilica of Bordeaux🔔
excerpt: Today we went to the Bell Tower of Saint Michael Basilica of Bordeaux. It was so much fun. First, Mommy and Puppy got coffee at a coffee shop. Then we walked towards the Bell Tower of Saint Michael Basilica of Bordeaux. We got tickets, and
body:
Today we went to the Bell Tower of Saint Michael Basilica of Bordeaux. It was so much fun. First, Mommy and Puppy got coffee at a coffee shop. Then we walked towards the Bell Tower of Saint Michael Basilica of Bordeaux. We got tickets, and this guide told us to go down to the crypt and look at it. So we looked at it for like a minute, and then we walked up .

There were so many stairs. There were exactly 230 stairs, and it was a spiraling staircase. There were some places where you could look outside, some air holes. The view was really great. When we were really high up, we saw all the bells that rang at 12. Then, when we were at halfway, there was a little space where you could see everywhere. It was kind of like the top. Like, do we still have to go up? Because we've already went for so long, and there were so many steps.

Then, when we got to the top, the view was amazing. We looked around for a bit. Mom took some photos, Puppy took some photos, and the view was great. We could see all these different places, and it looked like every single roof had shingles. We saw some people who had spaces on the top of the roofs where they could like hang out.

Then we saw these people using this booklet thing and looking at it. We went all the way to the end and found it. We saw how you would go all the way up. We were as high as you could go. So we got one of those booklet things, and we went over all these like amazing landmarks that you could see from the very top that you could go to.

Right after we got out of the tower, the bells started ringing, and we imagined how loud it must have been for the people who were still inside!

It was really fun. If you go to Bordeaux, you should definitely try it out. It was really great, but people six and under could not go.
author: ayana

title: The Abbey
excerpt: Yesterday, I went to an Abbey. We were stopping between Toulouse and Bordeaux. Right after going to this church, we went to this abbey and we checked it out. Mom went to go get her camera while Zarmina, Puppy, and I went inside. We got this
body:
Yesterday, I went to an Abbey. We were stopping between Toulouse and Bordeaux. Right after going to this church, we went to this abbey and we checked it out. Mom went to go get her camera while Zarmina, Puppy, and I went inside. We got this little booklet that was in English, thankfully, so Zarmina and I could both read it.

Then we walked through and looked at this grassy area in the middle with a tree. There was also an upstairs. Puppy told me that the things at the top of every single one of the pillars had something carved onto it, and they each tell a different story. So we looked at them, and Puppy told me the different stories of them. There were so many!

When Mom came, we walked around for a bit and checked out these cool places just to look around. Then I went into this room and watched a video about the church that we saw just before we saw this abbey.

Puppy asked me if we were ready to go. Mom was like, "Oh, have you guys seen upstairs?" and we were like, "Oh, no, we haven't." Puppy was like, "Oh, I'll take them." While Mom was taking photos, Puppy took us upstairs.

We walked upstairs; it wasn't that long. We saw that there was something going on, and we realized that it was the church that we were just in. There was a choir singing because something was going on. It was really pretty. We could see outside of these windows, and we watched them sing for a little bit.

Then we went back down and we left. It was really fun. I would definitely recommend it. If you are in that area, you should definitely check it out.
author: ayana

title: Fun in the Water Mirror🪞
excerpt: Yesterday we just finished eating our delicious food, and we walked down for a tiny bit to this humongous museum. I did not want to go in the sun because it was blazing hot. Then we saw this thing called the water mirror. Zarmina and I to
body:
Yesterday we just finished eating our delicious food, and we walked down for a tiny bit to this humongous museum. I did not want to go in the sun because it was blazing hot. Then we saw this thing called the water mirror. Zarmina and I took off our socks and shoes because that's what most people were doing.

The floor thing was nice and wet. It was a nice break from the heat, so we were sliding around, and there was a slight mist coming out of these things. It was really nice. Then we heard the water. Zarmina said that because she did an essay on Bordeaux, the water would rise in 15 minutes. So I waterskated around, meaning I slid around with my bare feet. It was really fun, and Zarmina joined me for a little bit, too.

Then we heard the water rushing, and we knew that it was going to come on soon. About 1 minute later, the water started rising. It felt so nice on my toes! Mom was just taking pictures of things, but she said that it was hard because of the glare of the sun. Puppy was watching us play. Once the water was at an okay level—not our whole feet were covered, but till the bottom of our ankles—we slid around, and it was so much fun.

But then, when I was chasing Zarmina, I fell. I did not get hurt because the water cushioned me, but I was not wearing a bathing suit, so my clothes got all soaked. I did not care because it was so hot. We kept playing and playing. At one point, Puppy and Mommy came in, and they were just standing still and getting their feet wet. They weren't getting their whole legs wet. Zarmina and I were running around, and I photobombed in every photo that she was in. It was so funny!

We stayed there for around 15 minutes playing, racing back and forth. Then we saw two people on scooters. They were riding around, and it looked like a lot of fun. The water was lowering, so Zarmina and I made sure that we would still waterskate around for the last bit. Once the water was all gone, we waited there for a few minutes, then the mist came back on. It was a nice mist, but I liked the water better.

We had so much fun, but since Zarmina and I were kicking and splashing each other, we were completely soaked. Once we were finished, I put my socks and shoes back on. Zarmina had quick dry shorts, but I was wearing jean shorts, so they would take a long time to dry, and my shirt did not dry that quickly. When I was walking around, it felt really nice that I had some cool clothes on. The water wasn't leaking, but it made the shorts and the shirt really heavy. The shirt soon quickly dried up, but my shorts stayed wet.

It was really fun. Once we got home, I let my shorts out to dry. I had a really fun time at the water mirror. I would definitely go back. It was so much fun. If you go to Bordeaux, you should definitely try it out. If you had toddlers or just in general kids, they'd love it.
author: ayana

title: Toulouse Capitole Paintings 🖼
excerpt: Today we went to the Toulouse Capitole. From the outside, it actually looks a bit like the White House, which makes sense because French buildings inspired a lot of famous American architecture back in the day. It has been the main heart
body:
Today we went to the Toulouse Capitole. From the outside, it actually looks a bit like the White House, which makes sense because French buildings inspired a lot of famous American architecture back in the day. It has been the main heart of Toulouse since all the way back in the 1100s. The eight big columns along the front were actually built to represent the Capitouls, who were the eight original leaders that ruled the city.

When you go inside, it stops looking like a plain old building and looks just like an actual royal palace. There are rooms and rooms of massive paintings lining the walls with gorgeous gold frames, and some are even painted right onto the ceilings! It must have taken artists years and years to finish all of this work. The big famous room called the Salle des Illustres is filled with artwork telling stories about history and mythology, which is why some of the people are naked, since that was just how classical art was done back then.

My absolute favorite painting was this super famous one done by an artist named Henri Martin. He used millions of tiny dots of paint to create the entire picture, which is just crazy looking when you see it up close! The way the sunlight lands on everyone and how the shadows were painted is so realistic. The gold frame really illuminates the sheep and makes them one of the main focuses of the whole painting. It looks like a sweet story of two people who are in love, enjoying the beautiful spring gardens, looking over their sheep together, and getting ready to spend a super happy life together. Seeing all these giant, story filled masterpieces up close was so awesome!
author: zarmina

title: Natural History Museum And Fun Exhibits 🌿
excerpt: Today we went to the Natural History Museum, where we saw this beautiful botanical garden. We explored all around and even found some cotton that Ayana stole! Then we went into the greenhouses. The tropical one was so humid that the air f
body:
Today we went to the Natural History Museum, where we saw this beautiful botanical garden. We explored all around and even found some cotton that Ayana stole! Then we went into the greenhouses. The tropical one was so humid that the air felt heavy, and there was so much moisture that water was dripping all over the plants. We also visited the desert greenhouse, which was bone dry and filled with cacti everywhere. They were all super prickly, and I was so tempted to touch them, but I resisted! We even saw a section with Venus flytraps that had a few dead flies trapped inside. I guess they were feeling hungry!

Next, we went to the minerals section and saw tons of amazing crystals and unique rocks. There was one really cool green mineral where a reaction made it look like it had bubbles all over it. Another rock was covered in sharp spikes that immediately made me think back to the cacti. We also saw a cool earthquake simulation replica. I already knew that earthquakes happen when two tectonic plates rub against each other. There were lava rocks too, which I thought were really cool. Plus a replica of the Earth showing all the different rock layers with descriptions in French. I had loads of fun exploring all the minerals, and we even got a sneak peek of the animal exhibit while we were there.

Since our tickets let us come and go whenever we pleased, we came back a little while later to properly explore the animal exhibit. We started off on the second floor, where they had realistic recreations of animals in their natural habitats. One was an otter in the water scavenging for fish on the far right side. Then we went down to the first floor and walked through a gorgeous butterfly exhibit. Mom saw a few butterflies that immediately reminded her of Africa, and they were all so pretty!

After that, we moved on to the birds and saw everything from huge feathers to the tiniest little birds and ones with the weirdest beaks. We saw an ostrich that brought back memories of a safari we went on where we saw an ostrich with an egg, and our guide asked if we wanted a massive omelet! Since we only had thirty minutes left before closing, we zoomed through the rest of the museum. We saw a bunch of cute wild cats that looked like the cat we saw on the train with the cool pattern on its coat. Then we saw some really weird rats, including one with a gross thick tail and another one that looked exactly like Peter Pettigrew from Harry Potter! We had so much fun exploring all these exhibits, and I would love to do it all over again.
author: zarmina

title: The Church near Bordeaux ⛪️
excerpt: Yesterday we went to this church on our way to Bordeaux. We were going to eat, but then we saw this humongous church, and we knew that we had to go in. The door was open, so we walked in. Outside the door, there was this amazing doorway. Th
body:
Yesterday we went to this church on our way to Bordeaux. We were going to eat, but then we saw this humongous church, and we knew that we had to go in. The door was open, so we walked in. Outside the door, there was this amazing doorway. The door was huge, and the doorway had all these little carvings on it. I didn't notice then, but each carving was very intricate and told a story of its own.

When we went inside, Puppy read us the plaque because we did not speak French, so he translated for us. We learned all about it. There was this beautiful statue, and we went into all the nooks and crannies and checked it out. There were these beautiful patterns on the walls, and I thought it looked beautiful.

Then, when I was looking around, I noticed that Mom had disappeared. This happened a lot when we were walking because she likes to take photos, which is really great. I was looking around, and they told me that she'd be out in the doorway. I looked in one doorway and I didn't see her, so I looked in the other.

That is when I noticed all the intricate designs. I noticed there were cat and dog sculpture things on the door staring at each other. There were also pigeons and other types of animals like that. There was this one thing where the design was so intricate. I imagined how hard it must have been to do such intricate details.

After that, we had some pasta at an Italian restaurant, and then we drove to Bordeaux. I definitely think if you ever go there, if you're ever in that area, you should definitely check it out.
author: ayana

title: Museum of Machines and the Minotaur
excerpt: Today we walked to the Museum of Machines, and the walk was super fun and beautiful. Our trail went right along the canal and was lined with a bunch of trees, so it was nice and shaded, which I was very grateful for! The walk was so peace
body:
Today we walked to the Museum of Machines, and the walk was super fun and beautiful. Our trail went right along the canal and was lined with a bunch of trees, so it was nice and shaded, which I was very grateful for! The walk was so peaceful because I was able to just gather my thoughts and daydream about how the rest of the day was going to go.

The moment I stepped into the exhibition area, I instantly loved it and knew it was going to be better than what I dreamed! We saw so many unique things. For example, there was a machine that literally rocked plants to sleep! There were a lot of crazy contraptions that you might think were random at first, like a machine that made an apple change colors. We even got to watch this amazing performance with a woman suspended on a rope. While hanging upside down, she used her head, arms, and legs to move through these rings made out of mist. It was crazy cool!

After that, we saw even more creations, including a machine that waters plants all by itself. Then the performer came back out, but this time the giant Minotaur from outside came indoors and she got super close to it. The Minotaur even sprayed people with water mist right out of its nostrils! Luckily we did not get wet, but near the end, we saw a guy who used a machine that shot real fire high into the air. The heat felt so intense that I cannot even imagine how hot it was for the people standing right next to it! The overall experience was so much fun, and it is definitely near the top of my list of favorites.
author: zarmina

title: Natural History Museum
excerpt: We went to a natural history museum a few days ago. We just finished going to this other museum, but it was full, so they said that the Natural History Museum would be good. Then, we walked to the Natural History Museum because it wasn't th
body:
We went to a natural history museum a few days ago. We just finished going to this other museum, but it was full, so they said that the Natural History Museum would be good. Then, we walked to the Natural History Museum because it wasn't that far.

After we got tickets, we went inside. First, we looked around this area where there were all these different things. Puppy read it aloud because it was in French, plus we don't speak French.

Next, we decided to go to the botanical gardens. We walked around for a bit. I found a cotton plant with cotton on it. So I took some of the cotton to feel how fluffy it was. It was very fluffy! While we were walking around for a little bit more, we saw this greenhouse with all these plants in it. But you could not touch the plants because they were like Venus fly traps, plus stuff like that.

Then we went to another part of another greenhouse to see all these gourds. After that, we went to a really humid greenhouse where all these rainforest plants were growing. It sounded like a rainforest, also felt like a rainforest. It was very humid with all these plants growing.

Later, we went over to a very, very hot greenhouse. It was for cacti. We didn't stay in there for long. Next, we went inside, then went into one of the exhibits on the first floor. It was an exhibit with gems plus rocks. Then, after it was finished, it caved. We walked a little bit farther until we saw an animal exhibit.

We walked around the animal exhibit for a little bit because there were so many animals. There were crocodiles, all types of birds, also a variety of different animals like goats, sheep, mammoths, foxes, bears, coyotes, dogs, cats, anteaters, armadillos, buffalo, baby elephants, koalas, sloths, plus kangaroos.

Right before, we had went to an exhibit where there was a few animals in the exhibit, but it was like a Native American exhibit where lots of things were there. But we also went to a natural disasters exhibit. We learned how an earthquake felt, plus all those kinds of stuff. We even saw a video of how volcanoes were made.
author: ayana

title: Painting Out In The Open Air 🎨🖌
excerpt: Yesterday we came upon this super cute little arts and crafts area! Even though it was closing when we first saw it, we got all the information we needed so we could go back the next day. So today, right after our chill time, we headed over
body:
Yesterday we came upon this super cute little arts and crafts area! Even though it was closing when we first saw it, we got all the information we needed so we could go back the next day. So today, right after our chill time, we headed over there. It was only a 3 minute walk from the house. The person running the place spoke very little English, but luckily another customer was able to translate for us.

We ended up doing acrylic painting, which was super different from watercolor. It was really fun looking around me to get inspiration from the flowers and animals around us. I had a bit of trouble with the body of my painting spreading too much at first, but after redoing it a few times, I finally got a shape I really liked. I filled in the background, though I decided to skip the flowers and grass since it was way too much work for the little bit of time we had left. Mom painted some flowers with a green background, but she did not really like how hers turned out. Ayana painted a dark castle and a tree with the ocean right below it, and she absolutely loved how hers turned out!

We also got to hang out with the customer who translated for us. Apparently she is a professional who creates 3D animations for a video game! Her painting was of a boy holding a star with a trail of glimmer (Ayana's idea), and she even used a template to make a cool pattern covering most of the boy's body. It was honestly one of my favorite memories in Toulouse!
author: zarmina

title: Art class🎨

body:
Today, Mom, Zarmina, and I went to a painting class. It was in the Royal Jardin. We were there the day before, and we decided to go that day. Puppy was doing stuff at a restaurant nearby because that was one of the only places that had Wi-Fi.

When we went to the painting class, the woman there did not speak English, so she was going to ask someone for help. Then the woman who was getting supplies was like, "Oh, I know English," and she also spoke French. And so she helped us find all our stuff and get us set up with all the painting stuff. We got some frames and some paints, and we started painting.

Zarmina used one of the stencils to make a capybara because she loves capybaras. Me and Zarmina, we love capybaras. And so she kind of just copied the stencil. She didn't actually use it. She was just copying the shape of the capybara just to look at the stencil.

And then Mom, she made this beautiful flower. I love the way she did the petals and the green background. And then the person who was helping us, she made a boy catching the star. She wanted to use glitter, so I gave her the idea to make a star trail, and later I thought that she should do the bottom with glitter. The glitter added an amazing touch when I saw the finished look. I thought it looked amazing.

And I made a castle with a sea and it was a rocky cliff, but first I made the dead tree. It was a very stormy place. I really liked it. If you go to Toulouse, you should definitely try it out.
author: ayana

title: Sushi 🍣 and Cheesecake 🍰
excerpt: Today Mom, Ayana, and I went to get dinner after walking around all day at the natural history museum. The waitress asked if we would be finished by 8:30, and since it was only 7:30, she clearly did not know how fast we eat! We ordered a sh
body:
Today Mom, Ayana, and I went to get dinner after walking around all day at the natural history museum. The waitress asked if we would be finished by 8:30, and since it was only 7:30, she clearly did not know how fast we eat! We ordered a shrimp tempura appetizer that was totally amazing.

For our main course, we got a crab, avocado, and cucumber roll topped with fish eggs, a tuna, cucumber, and avocado roll with green onions on top, and a salmon and avocado roll sprinkled with sesame seeds. Everything was fabulous, and my favorite was definitely that first roll!

That was not even the best part, because we got dessert! We ordered a Japanese style lemon cheesecake, which was the most popular dessert on the menu, and it had a really good reason to be. Cheesecake crust is usually a hard graham cracker, but this one had a soft crust that still held its shape perfectly. The filling had just the right balance of lemon and creaminess. It was honestly one of the best cheesecakes I have ever had!
author: zarmina

title: We went to a museum
excerpt: We went to a museum. In the museum, there was this bull riding around. It was a humongous mechanical bull. It was really cool to watch, and it was outside. When we went inside, we saw a lot of other structures like that, like a spider, and
body:
We went to a museum. In the museum, there was this bull riding around. It was a humongous mechanical bull. It was really cool to watch, and it was outside. When we went inside, we saw a lot of other structures like that, like a spider, and then we saw one humongous spider outside, too. There was so much to do in the museum!

First, we went over to this place where lots of people were surrounding it. It was someone making fire and stuff. A few minutes before the person doing the fire thing ended, we saw someone hanging from a rope from the ceiling. It was really cool. After the fire thing ended, the person went really high up, and then another person sent rings of smoke towards them. It was a really cool performance to watch.

Then, we went to a plant area where lots of plants were getting watered and stuff like that. We checked that out for a little bit, and then we went to this movie thing upstairs. Zermina and I watched one of the movies, and we watched two boxes come up from the ground. They were holding structures like the one that we saw outside, the bull. There was a crocodile and a fish. It was really cool to see what was happening.

We stayed there for a bit longer, then Puppy said that we should go down and see the person hanging from the ceiling. We already saw that before, and it was the same person. It looked like they were getting ready for something. Then, they started playing music, and the bull that we saw from outside rode in. There were people riding inside of it, and they were pointing to the person on the ceiling. The bull sprayed water from its nose, and the person was doing all these cool tricks on the rope.

Once it was done, we were finished with the museum because we went through a lot of things, and we also saw a few knickknacks. It was amazing to see how the people designed the bull, and it was crazy how big it was. The human must have been so brave doing acrobatics on the roof like that, hanging from a rope. I would not be able to do that.

I was really glad that we went to that museum, and I would definitely go there again to see more of those things. If you go to Toulouse, you should probably see it, too!
author: ayana

title: The Park: 🦆 🪿
excerpt: Today we went to the park and came across this duck family, and they were so cute! When another duck came too close to her duckling, the mother duck instantly attacked it to protect her baby. We also saw some ducks fighting over a crab be
body:
Today we went to the park and came across this duck family, and they were so cute! When another duck came too close to her duckling, the mother duck instantly attacked it to protect her baby. We also saw some ducks fighting over a crab because they were so hungry. The ducks here searching for food by diving underwater and wiggling their butts to reach deeper in the water. Some ducks just chill on this little house made for them, while others peacefully relax on the grass, totally unbothered by anything around them. One duck even yawned and stretched its wings out at the same time, which was incredibly cute! They swim around carefully examining the water for food, but pretty much all these ducks care about is eating and sleeping. They are just terribly cute!

There were also some geese that were doing their own thing, and they were super cute too. They looked so pretty swimming around on the water. I wondered if the two geese were partners or maybe a mother and baby, since one of them was quite a bit larger than the other. They completely did their own thing, not even giving the ducks a second glance even though they were sharing the same space. The geese seemed a bit more calm and controlled, mainly spending their time sleeping. It was so much fun exploring the park in Toulouse and finding all these cute birds. It is just so awesome getting to experience new things that we would never get to see if we had stayed back in the USA!
author: zarmina

title: Museum

We went up, and we saw these beautiful paintings on the ceilings and on the walls. They were very unique in their own way. I loved looking at them. You could look at them for hours!

When we finished going up the stairs, there were a few rooms after that. I looked at one of the rooms, and I stayed there for a little bit until I realized that there was another room. So, I went inside of that for just a tiny bit. Then I went into this other room for a little bit longer because there were so many paintings. We took photos of all the paintings. We could have definitely stayed there longer, but we had other things to do.

It was so pretty, and one of the paintings that we saw was three paintings combined. We got this little book explaining what was going on in the museum. So, I read the book and I learned all about the museum. It was a tiny little leaflet that I also used as a fan because it was super hot.

It was such a cool experience. If you go to Toulouse, you should definitely check it out.
author: ayana

We went to visit these gorgeous gardens, and unlike the ones in Marseille, it was not just regular plants everywhere. The colors of the flowers looked so beautiful together, and the blend of soft purples, yellowish browns, and light greens looked totally gorg. There was also a stunning fountain, and the water combined with all the flowers created the most perfect look and atmosphere. The vibe was just amazing, with everyone chilling on the grass, admiring the water fountain, and looking so grateful to be hanging out in such a beautiful place.

Then we saw all the different animals, which was so much fun. The roosters were walking around enjoying looking super superior, and there were loads of ducks that were really cute. The tiny baby ducks were eating and looking completely adorable, and there was even a majestic swan just sleeping peacefully. I even spotted a cool koi fish swimming right underneath one of the baby ducks. To make it even better, there was this total fairytale looking bridge surrounded by flowers that goes right over the river. There was also a waterfall that the pigeons absolutely loved playing in. It is just so great to be here surrounded by all this nature and positive energy.

Today we went to Carcassonne, and the moment we stepped out into the warm air, I could instantly tell it was going to be incredible. The flowers surrounding us and all the cute little houses and apartments were so pretty. When we first arrived, it was so peaceful with barely anyone around. We walked across a bridge that separates the old part of town from the new part, heading toward this giant medieval fortress where people actually still live today. It looked so crazy and majestic. The second I saw it, I immediately thought it looked like something straight out of a fairytale, just like Snow White. Actually, Walt Disney got inspiration for castles like Snow White and Sleeping Beauty from places just like this!

Once we went inside the walled city, we walked past all these cute markets and little shops before heading straight to the main castle area. The inside was so beautiful, with stunning statues and detailed mosaics everywhere. Then we went up to see the view, and it was completely breathtaking. You could see endless trees, petite houses, and if you looked really far off into the distance, you could even catch a tiny glimpse of the sea. After that, we went to this history camp where we learned about how heavy the old knights' armor was, and we learned about historical diseases like the Black Death, which killed 25 million people, a massive amount of people back then.

We also got to actually play the board game Carcassonne while being right inside Carcassonne, which was so much fun! Ayana ended up winning because she had Papa on her team, which was totally unfair, but it was still such a cool memory to play the game inside the actual castle itself.

T

oday we went to a museum and got to see this super cool fashion exhibit. I learned so much about sewing and how designers create all these different styles and textures in clothing. Most of the signs and descriptions were in French so I could not understand every single word, but I learned that the exhibit was all about a famous French designer named Mossi Traore. He is incredibly creative and uses his work to bring together all kinds of different cultures. It was fascinating to see how he designed actual soccer jerseys for teams and then turned right around to make stunning dresses for models to wear on the runway. He loves to draw inspiration from diverse heritages, especially Indian culture and traditional garments, and he blends those beautiful textile crafts into his modern masterpieces. It is so cool how he shapes these complex outfits just by draping and folding pieces of cloth together before sewing them up.

Even though some of the clothes and dresses he made were not exactly my personal fashion taste, it was still amazing to learn about how clothing is constantly evolving around the world. It really showed me how many unique styles and traditions of fashion exist across different cultures. Learning about all of this made me feel so much more appreciative of design, and it makes me super excited to discover even more unique types of fashion as we keep traveling to new places.

title: A Day at the Mucem!

During our time in Marseille, we decided to visit the Mucem. The moment we arrived, we passed by the main entrance for a bit and walked up to a beautiful, sun-drenched garden area overlooking the sea. We spent some time wandering through the greenery, soaking in the views, before heading down to the main ticketing area. After scanning our options, we decided to get tickets for a fashion exhibition that was currently on display.

As we stepped into the exhibit and began looking around, a specific display caught my eye: a large TV screen showcasing footage of a high-fashion runway show. I walked over to watch it closely. Some of the outfits were incredibly cute, and I found myself genuinely loving the designs. But sometimes the outfits were not my style. However, what fascinated me the most wasn't the clothing—it was the models' faces. They walked with absolute intensity, completely devoid of any emotion or expression. And some of the faces looked really funny to me.

After we were done watching the runway , we spent a little more time walking through the rest of the exhibit. We got to see the behind-the-scenes process and learned a lot about how the clothes were actually made, which was incredibly cool. Some of the more designs weren't really my style, and I didn't love every single piece on display. Still, the overall experience was fantastic. If you ever find yourself at the Mucem, I would definitely sa y you should go check it out!
